payload.name: Include Preference Memories for Like and Favorite Searches
payload.description: When a question asks what a person likes, prefers, or considers a favorite, do not restrict retrieval to profile memories; include preference memories when searching and before concluding no information.
content: When a question asks what someone likes, prefers, or considers a favorite, do not restrict retrieval to memory_kind 'profile'; include 'preference' memories because likes and favorites are often stored there.

For shared-interest questions (what do two people both like), run each person's search with preference-aware queries (e.g., '<name> prefers', '<name> favorite', '<name> likes') and compare the returned objects; if the first search yields no preference memory, repeat once without the memory_kind filter before concluding missing evidence.
Stop after one broadened search per person yields no relevant preference memory, then answer from visible evidence.

candidates.solves: Access agents answering shared-interest or preference questions may restrict searches to profile memories and miss preference memories, leading to false 'no information' answers. This skill ensures preference memory kind is included when searching what people like, prefer, or consider favorites, and when intersecting commonalities between two people.

payload.name: Object Purpose Retrieval with State Memories and Synonyms
payload.description: When a question asks what a specific object, device, tool, or wearable helps someone do, include state memories and synonym expansions for the object before answering.
content: If the question asks what a specific object (e.g., smartwatch, app, gadget) helps a person with, include memory kind 'state' in the search; the object's role is often stored as a state memory (e.g., 'uses a tracking tool that...').
Add synonym expansions for the object term (e.g., smartwatch → tracking tool, wearable, device, fitness tracker, watch) and search with those terms.
Before answering, verify that a retrieved memory explicitly links that object to the described function; do not infer functions from unrelated activity or event memories.
Stop once the object's function is found or one round of state/synonym searches yields no new distinct memory.

candidates.solves: Addresses retrieval failures when a question asks what a specific object or tool (e.g., smartwatch) helps a person do, but the memory stores that object under a generic descriptor (e.g., tracking tool) and as a state memory rather than an event or plan. Without this rule, the agent searches only event/plan kinds and misses the relevant state memory, then answers from unrelated activity memories.

payload.name: Include Event Kind for Favorite Preference
payload.description: When a question asks about a person's favorite or preferred thing, include memory_kind 'event' in the memory search alongside preference and profile.
content: When searching for a favorite/preferred item, style, dish, or activity, do not restrict memory_kinds to only 'preference' and 'profile'; include 'event' because direct favorite statements may be stored under event kind.
In at least one query, use the exact attribute asked (e.g., 'dance style', 'favorite dish') in addition to the person's name, so an explicit event-kind statement naming the favorite surfaces.
Once a memory explicitly states the favorite attribute, answer from it and stop; do not require a preference-kind memory or run additional searches.

candidates.solves: Retrieval failures where a person's favorite/preferred attribute is stored under memory_kind 'event' rather than 'preference', and the agent's memory-kind filter excludes event memories, causing it to miss the direct preference statement and answer with a generic topic instead of the specific favorite.

payload.name: Retrieve Professional Roles via Predicate Search
payload.description: Use when a question asks for a person's position, role, or title in a team, job, or signed contract, and the initial retrieval returns only generic activity memories.
content: If the question asks for a role/position tied to an event like signing, joining, hiring, or drafting, run an additional structured search for that person with memory_kind 'event' and predicate 'employment' (or 'membership') when available, using the event verb from the question in the query.

If structured filters are unsupported, run a hybrid or keyword search combining the person's name, the event verb (signed, joined, drafted, hired), and the attribute word (position, role, title); include common role values (e.g., forward, guard, manager) only if the first retry is inconclusive.

After retrieving any event memory, verify whether its content explicitly states the requested role/position before answering; if found, use it. Stop after at most two targeted retry searches to avoid over-expansion.

candidates.solves: When a question asks for a specific attribute like a person's position, role, or title tied to an event such as signing, joining, hiring, or drafting, the initial generic search may return only activity memories and miss the decisive event memory. This skill ensures a targeted structured or keyword search on the relevant event predicate (employment/membership) so the memory that directly states the attribute is retrieved.

payload.name: Excitement and Anticipation Event Retrieval
payload.description: When a question asks what a person is excited about, looking forward to, or anticipating (e.g., a new TV series, event, or release), include event/activity memory searches before concluding evidence is missing.
content: When the question asks what a person is excited about, looking forward to, or anticipating, do not limit the search to memory_kind=preference; the answer may be stored as an event/activity memory.

Include query variants with anticipation terms (excited about, looking forward to, upcoming, new, waiting for) together with the subject's name and the item type (e.g., TV series, movie, book, event).
If an initial preference-only search returns only general interests, run one additional hybrid or structured search with no memory_kind filter (or memory_kind=event) before answering.
Stop once a memory naming the specific upcoming item is retrieved; answer from visible evidence and do not keep expanding.

candidates.solves: Questions about what someone is excited about or looking forward to are often answered by event/activity memories (e.g., 'Tim is excited about the upcoming series X') rather than preference memories. Restricting retrieval to preference kind returns only general interests and misses the specific named item.

payload.name: Disambiguate creation dates from sharing memories
payload.description: When a question asks when someone made or created a named item and retrieval returns only sharing, mentioning, or favoriting memories, search for event memories of making/testing/creating before answering.
content: If a question asks when someone made/created a specific dish or item, treat only event memories describing the act of making, testing, baking, creating, cooking, or trying as evidence of the creation date; memories of sharing, mentioning, or liking the item reflect when it was discussed, not made.

After the first search, if the only explicit matches are sharing, preference, or plan memories, run a follow-up search for the person combined with creation verbs (made, tested, baked, created, cooked, tried) and generic descriptors (new recipe, treat, dessert, dish, project) without requiring the exact item name.

If a retrieved event memory describes a generic creation by the same person near a plausible time but omits the item name, inspect its source context to determine whether it refers to the asked-about item before using its date.
Stop once an event memory directly or via source context confirms the creation date, or after the creation-focused search returns no same-subject event; do not keep expanding indefinitely.

candidates.solves: Questions that ask when someone made or created a specific item often fail because retrieval returns memories where the item was shared, mentioned, or favored, and the agent mistakes those timestamps for the creation date. The actual creation event may be stored with generic wording (e.g., 'tested a new recipe') and is missed by keyword searches for the exact item name.

payload.name: Food Preference Retrieval via Recipes and Dishes
payload.description: Use when a question asks which food, meat, dish, ingredient, or cuisine a person prefers, likes, or favors; retrieve preference memories including recipes, dishes, and cooking-related terms.
content: When a question asks about a person's preferred food category (e.g., meat, vegetable, cuisine, ingredient), do not restrict queries to the category term alone; also run searches using the person's name with 'favorite recipe', 'favorite dish', 'cooking', 'kitchen', 'loves to eat', and 'likes'.
Filter for preference memories (especially predicate 'food') and treat a named recipe or dish containing the item as direct evidence of preference for that item.

If the first search returns only unrelated preferences (e.g., pets, activities), run at least one follow-up using recipe/dish terms before concluding no information; stop once a clear preference is found or after one such follow-up.

candidates.solves: Questions that ask for a person's preferred food item often fail because the evidence is stored as a named recipe, dish, or ingredient rather than with the category word (e.g., the meat word may appear only inside a named recipe or dish). This skill guides retrieval to include recipe and cooking-related preference terms so indirect food-preference memories are not missed.

payload.name: Broader memory kinds for attribute facts
payload.description: When a question asks for a factual attribute of a named entity (e.g., age, birthday, breed), use memory kinds beyond state, and retry without memory_kind filters if the first search is empty.
content: For attribute questions (age, birthday, color, breed, etc.), do not limit the search to memory_kinds=['state']; query across profile, relationship, state, and preference memory kinds, since the fact may be stored in any of them.
If the initial search returns no evidence for the attribute, run one additional search without a memory_kinds filter and with the entity name as a text keyword before answering 'no information'.
Stop after one expanded search if the attribute is found or no new candidates appear; avoid exhaustive repetition.

candidates.solves: Access Agent misses factual attribute facts (e.g., age, birthday) because it restricts searches to a single memory kind like 'state' and then answers 'no information' without retrying with broader filters, even though the fact may be stored in relationship, profile, or preference memories.

payload.name: Include State Memories for Action Questions
payload.description: When a question asks what someone did or did for someone/something, include memory kind 'state' in searches because completed actions may be stored as state memories (e.g., purchases, new possessions, resulting conditions).
content: When a question asks what a person did or what action they took, do not restrict retrieval to event and plan memory kinds; also include state (and profile/preference when relevant), because completed actions are often recorded as state memories (e.g., 'purchased X', 'got new Y', 'has Z').

After the first search, if no event/plan memory clearly answers the action, run a follow-up search using the same subject and action paraphrases (e.g., 'bought', 'got', 'purchased', 'provided', 'gave') without the event/plan filter, and include state kind.
Stop once a memory explicitly states the action or its resulting state is found; do not answer with unrelated activities just because they mention the same subject.

candidates.solves: When a question asks what someone did or what action they took, restricting retrieval to event or plan memories can miss the answer when the completed action is stored as a state memory (e.g., a purchase, a new possession, or a resulting condition). The agent should include state memories in such searches and run follow-up queries without the event/plan filter before answering.

payload.name: Broaden date-specific search after exact-date miss
payload.description: When a question asks about an event on a specific date and a date-filtered search returns no match, run one broader search without the exact date filter before answering 'No information available'.
content: When a question includes an explicit date but the first search (especially with a point-in-time filter) returns no matching memory, run a follow-up hybrid search that omits the restrictive date filter or uses a wide window (±7 days), using the question's subject plus event terms such as 'accepted', 'achievement', 'internship', or the relevant noun from the question.

Do not require the memory's world_start to equal the question date; the question date may refer to when the event was discussed. If the follow-up finds a memory matching the subject and event type, answer from it.
Stop after this single broadened search if no relevant memory is found; do not keep expanding to unrelated dates, topics, or subjects.

candidates.solves: This solves cases where a question specifies an event date but the relevant memory records a different date (e.g., the question uses the date the event was discussed rather than the event's start date), and an exact-date filtered search misses the memory. It adds a controlled broadening step to find such memories before concluding no information.

payload.name: Event-date retrieval from event memories only
payload.description: When a question asks when an event happened (e.g., when did X give/get Y for Z) and initial retrieval returns a non-event memory mentioning the item, do not use that memory's timestamp as the answer. Apply before answering.
content: If a 'when did X give/get Y' question retrieves a non-event memory (preference, relationship, profile) mentioning Y, treat its world_start as unreliable for the event date; search for an event memory about the giving using generic terms such as 'gave', 'gift', 'received', or the object category.
Run a structured or hybrid search restricted to memory_kind 'event' (or predicate 'gift'/'gave') if the first search did not return one, and answer using the event memory's world_start.
Stop once an event memory directly describing the transaction is found; do not infer the date from preferences or relationship memories.

candidates.solves: When a question asks for the date of an event (e.g., when did someone give/receive something), the agent may answer with the timestamp of a non-event memory (preference, relationship, profile) that merely mentions the item, confusing a memory's recorded date with the actual event date. This skill guides the agent to treat only event-memory timestamps as evidence and to search for the underlying event using gift/give terms when the initial retrieval only surfaces non-event mentions.

payload.name: Post-achievement celebration as rest and recovery
payload.description: When a question asks how someone celebrated an achievement or win, and explicit celebration memories are absent, search for subsequent rest, time off, or relaxing plans by that person around the event date.
content: If a question asks how X celebrated an achievement (win, award, promotion) and searches with 'celebrate' or 'celebration' return no direct answer, treat the celebration as an implicit post-event activity: run a hybrid search with X's name and post-event relaxation terms such as 'time off', 'day off', 'weekend', 'chill', 'relax', 'recharge', 'rest', combined with the event date or 'after'.

Apply a temporal filter so only memories at or after the event date are considered, and include planned future events and event/state memories; do not answer from pre-achievement socializing or unrelated tournament memories.
Stop after one or two such searches if a memory shows X relaxing or recharging around the event date, or after two searches with no same-subject post-event recovery memory.

candidates.solves: When asked how someone celebrated an achievement, retrieval often anchors on explicit celebration vocabulary and misses memories that describe the celebration as planned rest, time off, or relaxing with pets. This skill broadens the follow-up search to post-event recovery terms and temporal filters so the implicit celebration memory can be found.

payload.name: Broaden memory kinds for recent-activity questions
payload.description: Use when a question asks what someone recently finished, read, watched, or completed, possibly with a date, and an event-only search fails to find direct evidence.
content: If the question asks what someone recently finished/completed (e.g., 'just finished reading', 'recently watched'), do not restrict the search to memory kind 'event'; also include 'preference' and 'state' memories, since such completions are often stored there.

When the question includes a date but also uses 'recently' or 'just', do not require the memory's world_start to equal that exact date; accept memories dated within a plausible prior window (e.g., the preceding several weeks) and verify the completion wording.

After retrieving a candidate memory, confirm it explicitly states the completed activity (e.g., 'finished reading', 'recently read') and matches the subject; if it only describes interest or a plan, continue searching. Stop as soon as a direct completion memory is found.

candidates.solves: When a question asks what someone recently finished or completed (e.g., reading, watching, writing) and the initial search restricted to event memories returns no direct evidence, the correct evidence may live in a preference or state memory recorded with a relative time like 'recently' rather than an exact date. The agent should broaden memory kinds and relax strict date equality to recover such memories.

payload.name: Use Full Time Range for Month-Bounded Event Queries
payload.description: When a query asks about an event in a named month/year or broad time window, use time_mode range covering the whole window instead of a single point.
content: When a question asks about an event 'in [month] [year]' or another broad time window, set time_mode to 'range' with start and end covering the entire named period; do not use time_mode 'point' anchored to the first day because it can exclude events later in the month.

If the first range search does not surface a matching memory, run one broader retry: keep memory kinds 'event' and 'plan', add question-specific activity and invitee/participant terms, and widen the time window or omit it before concluding no information.
Stop after one or two retries once a memory matching the subject and event is retrieved.

candidates.solves: Queries that describe an event by a named month or broad time window often fail when the search anchors time_mode to a single point, excluding memories later in that window. This skill ensures month-bounded queries use a full-range time window and retry before answering no information.

payload.name: Current Activity Retrieval by Time Period
payload.description: Use when a question asks what a person is/was doing during a specific time period (month, year, season) and the first search returns no clear match.
content: If a question asks what a person is/was doing during a specific time period and the first search returns no clear state memory, rerun the search using the person's name plus generic activity terms (working, interning, studying, planning, taking a trip, etc.) while omitting the exact time phrase.

If that still misses, run one structured search filtered to memory_kind=state and subject=<person>; then check whether the returned memory's world_start/world_end interval covers the requested period.
Stop after one structured search or two hybrid retries, whichever comes first; do not expand indefinitely.

candidates.solves: When a question asks what a person is doing during a specific calendar period (e.g., June 2023, this summer), the agent often searches only the literal time phrase and misses stored state memories that describe the activity without a textual date. This skill provides a targeted retry strategy to retrieve active state memories for the person.

payload.name: Include plan memories for date-specific idea questions
payload.description: When a question asks what idea, plan, or initiative someone had on a specific date and initial retrieval returns no relevant memory, apply before answering no information.
content: When the question asks about an idea, plan, or initiative on a date and initial searches return no matching memory, rerun searches without restricting memory_kinds to event; include 'plan' (and 'state' or 'profile' when the idea is expressed as an intention or interest).
Use date-filtered structured and keyword searches with the person's name and the date, querying with terms such as plan, idea, initiative, volunteer program, or propose.
Stop once a memory with a world_start on or near the date answers the question; if none is found, answer no information without expanding to unrelated dates or topics.

candidates.solves: When a date-specific question asks about an idea, plan, or initiative someone had, retrieval may fail because searches are restricted to event memories even though the answer is stored as a plan memory. This skill ensures plan memories are included in date-filtered searches before concluding no information is available.

payload.name: Count events by target date with content-date fallback
payload.description: Use when a question asks how many events of a type occurred for a subject by a target date and searches may filter out memories whose world_start is after the target date.
content: When answering a count-as-of-date question, do not rely only on world_start filters; run at least one search with time_mode='none' (or a wide window) to find memories whose content may state the actual event date.

For each retrieved memory, resolve the event date from the content if it mentions one (e.g., 'on July 8, 2022', 'last week'), and count the event only if that content date is on or before the target date.

If a memory states an ordinal count (e.g., 'won his fourth tournament') but its world_start is after the target date, still include it when the content confirms the event happened before the target date; inspect all versions for the latest update.
Stop after one additional search without a time filter returns no new distinct event memories with content dates on or before the target date.

candidates.solves: Questions asking for a count of events by a target date can be answered incorrectly when a memory's world_start metadata is set to a later date (e.g., recording time) while the event date appears only in the content. Time-filtered searches then miss the decisive memory. This skill ensures retrieval includes content-embedded event dates and counts them correctly.

payload.name: Refine Broad Event Searches for Specific Activities
payload.description: Use when a time-period question asks about a specific activity and the first result is a broad trip or outing; search for concrete activities without date filters.
content: When a question asks what specific activity someone did during a given time period and the first overlapping memory describes only a broad event (trip, road trip, visit, outing), do not stop there. Run at least one additional hybrid search without the time filter, using the person's name and the broad event's main terms (e.g., Evan, road trip, Rockies), specifically looking for memories that name an activity.

If a follow-up memory names a concrete activity (e.g., skiing, hiking, kayaking) for the same person and appears to describe the same broad event, treat it as evidence even if its stored world_start/world_end does not overlap the requested period; the stored date may be the mention date rather than the event date.
Stop once a concrete activity is found, or after two follow-up searches yield no new concrete activity.

candidates.solves: When answering a time-bounded question about an activity, the agent may stop at a broad event memory (trip, visit) and miss the concrete activity stored in a related memory with a different timestamp, because the date filter excludes it. This skill instructs a follow-up search for event details without requiring date overlap.

payload.name: Resolve recent time frames before retrieval
payload.description: Use when a question asks about a 'recent', 'last', or 'this' weekend/activity/event, before searching resolve the relative time against the session timestamp and avoid hardcoding a past year.
content: When a question uses relative time words ('recent', 'last weekend', 'this weekend', 'latest'), resolve them against the session/message timestamp and set the search time window to that recent period (e.g., the last 14–30 days) ending at the session timestamp; do not hardcode a previous calendar year.
If a search is time-restricted and returns only older events, run one follow-up search without a time filter or with a widened recent window to capture the most current memory.

Before answering, confirm the candidate memory's date falls within the requested recency; if the only evidence is clearly older than 'recent', continue searching rather than answering from outdated memories.
Stop once a memory within the resolved recent window is found or after one widened follow-up yields no newer relevant memory.

candidates.solves: Retrieval fails when a question uses relative time words like 'recent weekend' but the search is constrained to a fixed past year, causing the agent to miss the most recent event and answer from older memories. This skill helps resolve relative time from the session timestamp and search with an appropriate recent window.

payload.name: Resolve bare month or season year from memory context
payload.description: When a question asks what someone did or visited in a month or season without a year, use the person's memory timeline to pick the year and search non-temporally first, instead of assuming the session year.
content: When a question time reference is a bare month or season (e.g., 'in May', 'last spring') without a year, do not use only the session timestamp to set the date range. First run a broad non-temporal search for the person and activity (with synonyms) to surface candidate memories, then check the month/season of each candidate.

If the broad search returns no candidate for the requested month, run a structured temporal search using the session year; if that yields no memory overlapping the month, retry once with the previous year (or the most frequent year in the person's retrieved memories) before concluding no evidence exists.
Accept a memory as evidence only if its world_start/world_end overlaps the requested month/season in one of the tried years; ignore memories whose month does not match even if other keywords align.
Stop after at most two temporal year attempts plus one non-temporal search; do not expand to exhaustive year sweeps.

candidates.solves: Questions that reference a month or season with no year often fail because the agent builds the date range from the current/session year, while the person's relevant memories are from an earlier year. The skill forces a broad non-temporal search first and then a small set of plausible-year temporal searches so the right memory can be found without exhaustive year scanning.
